headline: Weekend Brief: Quiet weekend keeps US markets focused on chip-stock overhang, higher oil and mixed consumer and housing signals ahead of LEI data and earnings
raw_text:
- Friday’s chip-stock selloff on AI spending concerns and rising Chinese AI competition remains a key overhang for US tech into Monday’s open
- Escalating Middle East tensions that pushed crude oil (@CL) higher could pressure energy-sensitive sectors and oil-linked equities
- Rising US foreclosures — over 227,000 filings in the first half of 2026, up 21% year over year and the highest since 2019 — highlight consumer stress and may refocus attention on real estate, homebuilder and distressed-asset names
- World Cup-related strength, including Bank of America data showing June US consumer spending at its fastest growth in four years and heavy betting volumes, may support consumer discretionary and retail stocks
- Adidas’ push to capitalize on World Cup momentum puts global sportswear and event-linked consumer names in focus
- The Conference Board Leading Economic Index for June, due at 10:00 AM ET, will be parsed for fresh US growth signals amid mixed manufacturing data
- Steel Dynamics (STLD) reports earnings Monday, offering insight into industrial demand, steel pricing and capital spending trends
- AMC Entertainment (AMC) reports earnings Monday, providing an update on box-office momentum and theater traffic
- Concerns over CLO profit pressures and the S&P 500 (SPY) breaking from typical earnings-season patterns add to broader equity-market risk considerations
- Ongoing Federal Reserve communication and rate-hike speculation remain in focus as relatively stable Asian and European trading is monitored for directional cues on tech and oil into the US open
